reasoning_traces.think:
The paper establishes a principled framework for uncertainty quantification in deep spatiotemporal models using statistical decision theory. The Mean Interval Score (MIS) emerges as a proper scoring rule for interval forecasts, minimizing expected interval width subject to coverage constraints. This dual role of MIS—balancing sharpness and calibration—aligns with GSE’s need for precise yet reliable interval forecasts. Frequentist methods like quantile regression and MIS regression offer strong coverage guarantees, while Bayesian approaches such as SG-MCMC excel in mean prediction accuracy. The authors demonstrate that MIS regression outperforms bootstrap and MC dropout in terms of both coverage and sample efficiency. In particular, MIS regression is recommended for GSE’s interval forecasting pipeline due to its computational tractability and theoretical grounding. The spline quantile approach offers an alternative when smoothness and monotonicity are required, especially in multi-quantile banding. These primitives form the basis of GSE’s next-generation uncertainty engine, integrating empirical risk minimization with probabilistic forecasting principles.
